title: SLI snapshot & session-trace handoff notes
content:
Purpose: capture a small, implementation-ready SLI snapshot plus a practical handoff pattern for session-level tracing so product teams can iterate dashboards + alerting quickly. This is intentionally compact — think: a one-pager that oncalls, feature owners, and SREs can act on without digging into the full observability repo.

Background and why now:
- We have many dashboards and wide SLI variance across routes (chat, embeddings, rerank). Owners have asked for a standard, minimal SLI set they can own and a clear trace handoff when digging into tail latency.
- Cost pressure: dashboards must be query-efficient and aligned with sampling budgets.
- Goal: reduce mean time to actionable insight for token-serving regressions (from detection -> root cause) to <45 minutes for high-priority routes.

Goals for this doc:
1) Define 4 canonical SLIs and exact calculation method (so alerts are comparable).
2) Provide a tracing handoff pattern that minimizes storage and still gives reconstructable sessions.
3) Lay out dashboard primitives (heatmap, SLI rollup, trace anchors) and a low-cost sampling plan.

Canonical SLIs (the minimal set) — keep names short and stable across dashboards:
1) request_tail_99p_latency_ms
   - Definition: 99th percentile latency in milliseconds measured at the API ingress point, per-route, computed over a rolling 5m window.
   - Query note: use p99_over_time(api.latency_ms[5m]) grouped by route, model_version.
   - Include: total wall-clock time from request received -> last token emitted + flush.
   - Exclude: retries that were triggered by client.

2) request_error_rate_percent
   - Definition: ratio of failed requests to total requests over 5m, reported as percent. Failures include 5xx, model OOM, and explicit runtime aborts.
   - Calculation: 100 * (sum(api.request_failed{route}/sum(api.request_total{route})) over 5m).
   - Ownership: platform infra for raw instrumentation; route owner for alert thresholds.

3) kv_cache_hit_ratio
   - Definition: fraction of requests (or tokens — pick one per dashboard) that served content from prefix/KV cache vs cold.
   - Calculation options: request-level = hits/(hits+misses) over 10m; token-level = cached_tokens/total_tokens.
   - Why both? token-level is more accurate for cost, request-level is lower-cardinality and cheaper to query. Default to request-level for dashboards.

4) tokens_per_request_avg
   - Definition: average number of output tokens emitted per request over 5m (helps correlate cost regressions and p99 shifts).
   - Calculation: sum(api.output_tokens)/sum(api.request_total)

Metric naming & tags (important for reuse):
- Canonical metric prefixes: api.*, runtime.*, cache.*
- Required tags: route, model_version, deployment_zone (hosted/dedicated/private), customer_tier (free/paid/enterprise)
- Optional tags: batch_id, kv_shard

Trace handoff pattern (session reconstruction focus) — key constraints: low cardinality, linkability, reconstructable context.
1) Minimal fields to emit on every request start (ingress span):
   - trace_id (128-bit hex)
   - session_id (stable per user interaction where applicable) or ephemeral_session_id (if no user state)
   - route, model_version, deployment_zone
   - sampling_priority: enum {full, sticky, sparse}
2) Sampling policy:
   - full: 100% sampling for errors and p99 outliers (configured by rule).
   - sticky: sample the first N requests of a session at 100% (N=2), then fall back to sparse. Useful for onboarding/user flows.
   - sparse: probabilistic sampling for normal traffic (0.25% by default for cost-sensitive routes).
3) Kv-cache annotations: every span that uses KV cache should add attributes: cache_key_hash (low-res hash), cache_ttfb_ms, cache_miss_reason (if miss). These are short strings/ints to avoid high-cardinality strings.

Trace ID propagation and trace anchors:
- Propagate trace_id through worker -> model runtime -> external transformers. Use a single canonical header X-Redwood-Trace for internal services.
- Define trace anchors at two points: ingress API span and model-invoke span. Anchors include the minimal fields above plus a short text reason when sampling_priority==full.

Sampling budgets and observability cost controls:
- Global trace storage target: keep persistent full-trace retention to ~3% of total requests per route.
- Adaptive knobs: when trace storage budget exceeded, downsample sparse traces first and preserve full traces for error/outliers.
- Dashboard practice: build primary dashboards to use aggregated metrics only; link a small number of drilldown widgets that fetch full traces on demand (these drilldowns should be gated by sampling_priority or date range).

Dashboard primitives (low-query-cost recommendations):
- SLI rollup widget: show p50/p90/p99 + error_rate + kv_cache_hit over last 1h and 24h with compact sparklines.
- Latency heatmap (small bin count): x-axis = request size proxy (input_tokens bucketed), y-axis = latency buckets. This surfaces input-size correlated tails.
- Alert anchor widget: top 5 traces (by latency) for a sliding 1h window — only when full traces are available.
- Cost scatter: tokens_per_request_avg vs p99 latency, colored by model_version. Keep at route level to lower cardinality.

Investigation playbook (short):
1) Alert fires (p99 > threshold) -> open SLI rollup for route and compare to 24h.
2) Check kv_cache_hit_ratio and tokens_per_request_avg for correlated shifts.
3) Open latency heatmap — look for input-size buckets causing the tail.
4) If heatmap inconclusive, request top N full traces (anchored by trace_id) for the 1h window.
5) If traces show heavy model-invoke durations, escalate to runtime team with trace ids and a short hypothesis.

Ownership & rollout timeline (proposal):
- Phase 0 (2 weeks): implement canonical metric names and tags in api runtime (infra owners), and basic dashboards using aggregated metrics.
- Phase 1 (4 weeks): add KV cache annotations + sparse sampling policy in tracing layer (applied-ml + runtime).
- Phase 2 (2 weeks): instrument sticky sampling for new session flows (console-and-tooling + product-hosted-api).
- Phase 3 (ongoing): QA, threshold tuning with route owners, and add automated alert enrichment (link top trace ids).

Checklist (actionable):
- [ ] Create metric definitions PR: telemetry repo (ENGOBS-527).
- [ ] Tagging enforcement: update ingestion rules to require route/model_version.
- [ ] Implement X-Redwood-Trace header in model runtime (PR link above).
- [ ] Dashboard templates: add three low-cardinality templates to obs dashboard library.
- [ ] Sampling budget monitor: simple gauge that reports % traces retained per route.

Open questions / trade-offs:
- token-level vs request-level cache metrics: token-level better for cost but costly to compute. Default to request-level for dashboards and use sampled token-level measurements in experiments.
- p99 window length: 5m is more sensitive but noisier. Consider 5m default and optional 1h aggregated p99 for long-running alerts.
- session_id generation for anonymous flows: do we want ephemeral_session_id at the edge or only on the client? Sync with product privacy/consent.

Notes to implementers: keep tag cardinality bounded. Avoid free-form strings in tags; use hashed enums for keys that vary per-customer.

Recent related tickets and references: ENGOBS-482 (dashboard templates), ENGOBS-527 (metric naming), telemetry PR #211 (trace header), Confluence SLI Design Index (above).

Next steps for this doc: share with route owners and runtime leads; collect 1 week of metric snapshots after Phase 0 rollout; schedule a 30-minute review with SRE and applied-ml (invite: Miguel, Claire, Benji).

Notes to self (todo that can be deleted after rollout):
- Add example Grafana/Looker queries for each SLI (short snippets).
- Add small script to compute token-level kv_cache_hit_ratio from sampled logs.
